paragraphs.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים אֵ֚ין מִלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אֲרָ֖ם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And they continued three years without war between Aram and Yisra'el.

notes.official: Aram = the Aramean kingdom of Damascus; Yisra'el = Israel. *wayyēšəḇû* 'And they continued', literally 'sat'. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the introduction.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑ית וַיֵּ֛רֶד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass in the third year that Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah came down to the king of Yisra'el.

notes.official: Yehoshafat = Jehoshaphat; Yehudah = Judah. The 'king of Yisra'el' is unnamed through most of the story and named Ach'av only at vv 20 and 39-40; many critics think the narrative was originally anonymous (Cogan).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־עֲבָדָ֔יו הַיְדַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־לָ֖נוּ רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ מַחְשִׁ֔ים מִקַּ֣חַת אֹתָ֔הּ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָֽם׃

i18n.en: And the king of Yisra'el said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramot-Gil'ad is ours, and we are still, and do not take it out of the hand of the king of Aram?"

notes.official: Ramot-Gil'ad = Ramoth-gilead, a fortress town east of the Yarden. *waʾănaḥnû maḥšîm* 'and we are still', i.e. doing nothing.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֛י לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּמ֧וֹנִי כָמ֛וֹךָ כְּעַמִּ֥י כְעַמֶּ֖ךָ כְּסוּסַ֥י כְּסוּסֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And he said to Yehoshafat, "Will you go with me to battle at Ramot-Gil'ad?" And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisra'el, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

notes.official: *kāmônî ḵāmôḵā kəʿammî ḵəʿammeḵā kəsûsay kəsûseyḵā* 'I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses': a formula of alliance (also 2 Kgs 3:7).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דְּרָשׁ־נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת־דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisra'el, "Inquire first, I pray you, for the word of YHWH."

notes.official: *dəraš-nāʾ ḵayyôm ʾeṯ-dəḇar YHWH* 'Inquire first, I pray you, for the word of YHWH': *drš* is the technical verb of consulting an oracle (central `darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle`, which cites vv 5-8). *kayyôm* 'first' (cf. 1:51).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ץ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֶֽת־הַנְּבִיאִים֮ כְּאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת אִישׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם הַאֵלֵ֞ךְ עַל־רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ עֲלֵ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: Then the king of Yisra'el gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall I go against Ramot-Gil'ad to battle, or shall I forbear?" And they said, "Go up; for the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."

notes.official: *wayyōʾmərû ʿălēh wəyittēn ʾăḏōnāy* 'And they said, Go up; for the Lord will give it': the four hundred use *ʾăḏōnāy* 'the Lord', not the Tetragrammaton, while Yehoshafat asks for 'a prophet of YHWH' (v 7); at v 12 they say 'YHWH'. Many Hebrew manuscripts read YHWH here. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`); some commentators see the contrast as deliberate (Gray; De Vries, *1 Kings*, WBC 12, 1985). The Hebrew names neither the object ('it') nor which king, an ambiguity often noted in the oracle.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֥ה נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה ע֑וֹד וְנִדְרְשָׁ֖ה מֵאוֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: But Yehoshafat said, "Is there not here a prophet of YHWH besides, that we may inquire of him?"

notes.official: *hăʾên pōh nāḇîʾ laYHWH ʿôḏ* 'Is there not here a prophet of YHWH besides': Yehoshafat distrusts the unanimous four hundred (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ׀ אֶֽל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט ע֣וֹד אִישׁ־אֶחָ֡ד לִדְרֹשׁ֩ אֶת־יְהוָ֨ה מֵאֹת֜וֹ וַאֲנִ֣י שְׂנֵאתִ֗יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא־יִתְנַבֵּ֨א עָלַ֥י טוֹב֙ כִּ֣י אִם־רָ֔ע מִיכָ֖יְהוּ בֶּן־יִמְלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט אַל־יֹאמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And the king of Yisra'el said to Yehoshafat, "There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of YHWH, Mikhayehu the son of Yimlah; but I hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil." And Yehoshafat said, "Let not the king say so."

notes.official: Mikhayehu = Micaiah ('who is like Yah?'); Yimlah = Imlah. *lōʾ-yiṯnabbēʾ ʿālay ṭôḇ kî ʾim-rāʿ* 'he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־סָרִ֖יס אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַהֲרָ֖ה מִיכָ֥יְהוּ בֶן־יִמְלָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then the king of Yisra'el called an officer and said, "Bring quickly Mikhayehu the son of Yimlah."

notes.official: *sārîs* 'an officer' (central `saris-court-official-eunuch-ambiguity`).

paragraphs.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֡ה יֹשְׁבִים֩ אִ֨ישׁ עַל־כִּסְא֜וֹ מְלֻבָּשִׁ֤ים בְּגָדִים֙ בְּגֹ֔רֶן פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְכָ֨ל־הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Now the king of Yisra'el and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah were sitting each on his throne, arrayed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomron; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

notes.official: *yōšəḇîm ʾîš ʿal-kisʾô ... bəḡōren peṯaḥ šaʿar šōmərôn* 'sitting each on his throne ... at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomron' (ASV 'in an open place'; KJV 'in a void place'). *gōren* is a threshing floor (BDB; HALOT). A large flat floor by the city gate served as a public place for royal and judicial business: in the Ugaritic Aqhat epic Danel judges 'at the entrance of the gate ... on the threshing floor' (KTU 1.17 V 6-8; cf. 2 Sam 24:16-25). The ASV paraphrase is replaced by the lexical sense (`goren-threshing-floor-1-kings-22-10`); the Hebrew is anarthrous, and English 'the' marks the known floor by the gate. The two kings enthroned with prophets before them are mirrored by YHWH enthroned with his host in v 19.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥ה בֶֽן־כְּנַעֲנָ֖ה קַרְנֵ֣י בַרְזֶ֑ל וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵ֛לֶּה תְּנַגַּ֥ח אֶת־אֲרָ֖ם עַד־כַּלֹּתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And Tzidqiyahu the son of Kena'anah made himself horns of iron, and said, "Thus says YHWH: 'With these you shall push Aram until they are consumed.'"

notes.official: Tzidqiyahu = Zedekiah; Kena'anah = Chenaanah. The MT writes the short form *ṣiḏqiyyâ* here and the long form at v 24; both are normalized to Tzidqiyahu (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *qarnê ḇarzel* 'horns of iron': a symbolic act that enacts the oracle (cf. the horns of the wild ox that 'push the peoples', Deut 33:17); *tənaggaḥ* 'you shall push' is the verb for goring.

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־הַנְּבִאִ֔ים נִבְּאִ֥ים כֵּ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲלֵ֞ה רָמֹ֤ת גִּלְעָד֙ וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, "Go up to Ramot-Gil'ad and prosper; for YHWH will give it into the hand of the king."

notes.official: The prophets now use the name YHWH (cf. v 6).

paragraphs.text: וְהַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֣ךְ ׀ לִקְרֹ֣א מִיכָ֗יְהוּ דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה־נָ֞א דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים פֶּֽה־אֶחָ֥ד ט֖וֹב אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ יְהִֽי־נָ֣א דבריך [דְבָרְךָ֗] כִּדְבַ֛ר אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶ֖ם וְדִבַּ֥רְתָּ טּֽוֹב׃

i18n.en: And the messenger who went to call Mikhayehu spoke to him, saying, "Behold now, the words of the prophets with one mouth are good to the king; let your word, I pray you, be like the word of one of them, and speak good."

notes.official: *wəhammalʾāḵ* 'And the messenger', a human envoy. Ketiv *dbryk* 'your words', Qere *dəḇārəḵā* 'your word'; the Qere is translated, as in the ASV (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *peh-ʾeḥāḏ* 'with one mouth', unanimously.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִיכָ֑יְהוּ חַי־יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֠י אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And Mikhayehu said, "As YHWH lives, what YHWH says to me, that will I speak."

notes.official: *ḥay-YHWH* 'As YHWH lives' (central `chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`, which cites this verse).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבוֹא֮ אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֵלָ֗יו מִיכָ֙יְהוּ֙ הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל־רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־נֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ עֲלֵ֣ה וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Mikhayehu, shall we go to Ramot-Gil'ad to battle, or shall we forbear?" And he said to him, "Go up and prosper; and YHWH will give it into the hand of the king."

notes.official: Mikhayehu first repeats the four hundred word for word ('Go up and prosper'); the king's reaction in v 16 shows that he hears it as irony.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־כַּמֶּ֥ה פְעָמִ֖ים אֲנִ֣י מַשְׁבִּעֶ֑ךָ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־תְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י רַק־אֱמֶ֖ת בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the king said to him, "How many times shall I adjure you that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of YHWH?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפֹצִ֣ים אֶל־הֶהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לֹֽא־אֲדֹנִ֣ים לָאֵ֔לֶּה יָשׁ֥וּבוּ אִישׁ־לְבֵית֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And he said, "I saw all Yisra'el scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd; and YHWH said, 'These have no master; let them return each man to his house in peace.'"

notes.official: *kaṣṣōʾn ʾăšer ʾên-lāhem rōʿeh* 'as sheep that have no shepherd' (cf. Num 27:17): the shepherd is the king, whose death is foretold. *lōʾ-ʾăḏōnîm lāʾēlleh* 'These have no master' (plural of majesty *ʾăḏōnîm*).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט הֲלוֹא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֽוֹא־יִתְנַבֵּ֥א עָלַ֛י ט֖וֹב כִּ֥י אִם־רָֽע׃

i18n.en: And the king of Yisra'el said to Yehoshafat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־יְהוָה֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ וְכָל־צְבָ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Therefore hear the word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing by him, on his right hand and on his left.

notes.official:
*lāḵēn šəmaʿ dəḇar-YHWH* 'Therefore hear the word of YHWH'. *rāʾîṯî ʾeṯ-YHWH yōšēḇ ʿal-kisʾô* 'I saw YHWH sitting on his throne': the prophet claims to have stood in YHWH's council (*sôḏ*), the mark of the true prophet at Jer 23:18, 22; the scene parallels Isa 6:1-8 and Job 1:6-12 (central `divine-council-phr-mad-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible` cites this verse).

*wəḵol-ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim ʿōmēḏ ʿālāyw mîmînô ûmiśśəmōʾlô* 'and all the host of the heavens standing by him, on his right hand and on his left'. *ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim* is the heavenly retinue here (new central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus`); elsewhere the same phrase names the stars as objects of worship (Deut 4:19; 2 Kgs 17:16; 21:3, 5). 'Host' (ASV) is kept, the noun of 'captain of the host' at 1:19 and 2:32, 35. *šāmayim* is rendered 'heavens' because the phrase here names the court around YHWH's throne in his dwelling (cf. 8:30), a divine-realm use for which genesis-woh also has 'heaven(s)' (GEN-WOH-28:12) (central `shamayim`). The plural keeps the Hebrew form; the ASV and the English edition of *The Book Which Tells the Truth* have the singular 'the host of heaven'. The weather and fire sites (18:45; 2 Kgs 1:10-14) keep 'skies'.

*ʿōmēḏ ʿālāyw* 'standing by him' (ASV; French edition of *The Book Which Tells the Truth* 'se tenant près de lui'): with verbs of standing, *ʿal* denotes attendants standing over or beside a seated superior (Gen 18:8; Judg 3:19; Zech 4:14; BDB s.v. *ʿal*), so 'by him' renders the idiom and 'over him' is its literal spatial sense. The singular participle agrees with the collective *ṣāḇāʾ*. The scene mirrors v 10.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him') as the prophet's vision of the creators. The line renders the Hebrew as the major versions do and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה מִ֤י יְפַתֶּה֙ אֶת־אַחְאָ֔ב וְיַ֕עַל וְיִפֹּ֖ל בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר זֶה֙ בְּכֹ֔ה וְזֶ֥ה אֹמֵ֖ר בְּכֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said, 'Who will entice Ach'av, that he may go up and fall at Ramot-Gil'ad?' And one said this way, and another said that way.

notes.official: *mî yəp̄atteh ʾeṯ-ʾaḥʾāḇ* 'Who will entice Ach'av': Piel of *pth* 'persuade, entice, deceive' (vv 20-22; Jer 20:7; Ezek 14:9; HALOT). The ASV 'entice' is kept: it names persuasion toward a fall without choosing between 'persuade' and 'deceive', and vv 22-23 make the deception explicit. On the theological problem, see J. J. M. Roberts, 'Does God Lie? Divine Deceit as a Theological Problem in Israelite Prophetic Literature' (VTSup 40, 1988). Ach'av = Ahab, named here for the first time in the chapter. *zeh bəḵōh wəzeh ʾōmēr bəḵōh* 'And one said this way, and another said that way': the council deliberates.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָר֗וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֣י אֲפַתֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו בַּמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the ruach came forth and stood before YHWH, and said, 'I will entice him.' And YHWH said to him, 'By what means?'

notes.official:
*wayyēṣēʾ hārûaḥ* 'And the ruach came forth' (ASV 'there came forth a spirit'). The Hebrew has the article. Hebrew can use the article for a single figure not yet introduced (GKC §126q-r), which is how the ASV and most versions read it ('a spirit'); it can also mark a known figure, and the rabbinic tradition identifies 'the spirit' as Navot's (b. Sanh. 89a), while JPS 1917 renders 'there came forth the spirit'. The translation keeps the article and the transliteration 'ruach' so that the word stays visibly the same in 'a lying ruach' (vv 22-23) and in Tzidqiyahu's retort about the *rûaḥ-YHWH* (v 24) (`ha-ruach-ruach-sheqer-the-ruach-and-the-lying-ruach-1-kings-22`, inferred; `ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`). The ruach is a member of the council standing 'before YHWH', as *haśśāṭān*, also with the article, is in Job 1:6. *ʾăp̄attennû* 'I will entice him'.

Versification: MT v 21 ends with YHWH's question *bammâ* 'By what means?'; the ASV and other English versions begin v 22 with it (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵצֵא֙ וְהָיִ֙יתִי֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל־נְבִיאָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּפַתֶּה֙ וְגַם־תּוּכָ֔ל צֵ֖א וַעֲשֵׂה־כֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And he said, 'I will go forth, and I will be a lying ruach in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he said, 'You shall entice him, and you shall also prevail; go forth and do so.'

notes.official:
*ʾēṣēʾ wəhāyîṯî rûaḥ šeqer bəp̄î kol-nəḇîʾāyw* 'I will go forth, and I will be a lying ruach in the mouth of all his prophets' (ASV 'a lying spirit', as in the English edition of *The Book Which Tells the Truth*; French edition 'un esprit de mensonge'). *rûaḥ šeqer* is literally 'a ruach of falsehood', a genitive of quality rendered adjectivally as in the ASV (GKC §128p) (`ha-ruach-ruach-sheqer-the-ruach-and-the-lying-ruach-1-kings-22`). *təp̄atteh wəḡam-tûḵāl* 'You shall entice him, and you shall also prevail'. ASV v 22 begins one clause earlier (v 21).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse and reads the scene as the creators using a 'group telepathy' so that none of the prophets would tell the king the truth. The line renders the Hebrew lexically: it names a ruach of the council and describes no mechanism.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל־נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ רָעָֽה׃

i18n.en: Now therefore, behold, YHWH has put a lying ruach in the mouth of all these your prophets; and YHWH has spoken evil concerning you."

notes.official: *nāṯan YHWH rûaḥ šeqer bəp̄î kol-nəḇîʾeyḵā ʾēlleh* 'YHWH has put a lying ruach in the mouth of all these your prophets' (v 22). By disclosing the deception to the king, Mikhayehu leaves him free to choose (R. W. L. Moberly, 'Does God Lie to His Prophets?', *HTR* 96, 2003).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶֽן־כְּנַעֲנָ֔ה וַיַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת־מִיכָ֖יְהוּ עַל־הַלֶּ֑חִי וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵי־זֶ֨ה עָבַ֧ר רֽוּחַ־יְהוָ֛ה מֵאִתִּ֖י לְדַבֵּ֥ר אוֹתָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Then Tzidqiyahu the son of Kena'anah came near and struck Mikhayehu on the cheek, and said, "Which way did the ruach of YHWH pass from me to speak to you?"

notes.official: *ʾê-zeh ʿāḇar rûaḥ-YHWH mēʾittî lədabbēr ʾôṯāḵ* 'Which way did the ruach of YHWH pass from me to speak to you?' (ASV 'the Spirit of Jehovah'). Tzidqiyahu claims for himself the same *rûaḥ* that vv 21-23 have just placed in the prophets' mouths. The transliteration keeps that link visible, and the lower case avoids the ASV capital, which presupposes the later doctrine of a personal Holy Spirit (`ruach-yhwh-and-prophetic-ruach-transliteration-kings`, extended here to the ruach of prophetic inspiration; cf. 2 Kgs 2:9, 15). MT long form Tzidqiyahu (v 11).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ הִנְּךָ֥ רֹאֶ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֛א חֶ֥דֶר בְּחֶ֖דֶר לְהֵחָבֵֽה׃

i18n.en: And Mikhayehu said, "Behold, you shall see on that day, when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself."

notes.official: *ḥeḏer bəḥeḏer* 'an inner chamber', literally 'a room within a room' (cf. 20:30).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קַ֚ח אֶת־מִיכָ֔יְהוּ וַהֲשִׁיבֵ֖הוּ אֶל־אָמֹ֣ן שַׂר־הָעִ֑יר וְאֶל־יוֹאָ֖שׁ בֶּן־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And the king of Yisra'el said, "Take Mikhayehu, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Yo'ash the king's son;

notes.official: Amon, *śar-hāʿîr* 'the governor of the city'; Yo'ash 'the king's son', possibly the title of an official rather than a son (Cogan).

paragraphs.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־זֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית הַכֶּ֑לֶא וְהַאֲכִילֻ֨הוּ לֶ֤חֶם לַ֙חַץ֙ וּמַ֣יִם לַ֔חַץ עַ֖ד בֹּאִ֥י בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: and say, 'Thus says the king: "Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace."'"

notes.official: *leḥem laḥaṣ ûmayim laḥaṣ* 'bread of affliction and water of affliction' (ASV), i.e. short prison rations; *laḥaṣ* is 'pressure, oppression'. *ʿaḏ bōʾî ḇəšālôm* 'until I come in peace': the king expects to refute the 'in peace' of v 17.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ אִם־שׁ֤וֹב תָּשׁוּב֙ בְּשָׁל֔וֹם לֹֽא־דִבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

i18n.en: And Mikhayehu said, "If you return at all in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, you peoples, all of you."

notes.official: *ʾim-šôḇ tāšûḇ bəšālôm lōʾ-ḏibber YHWH bî* 'If you return at all in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me': the test of Deut 18:22. *wayyōʾmer šimʿû ʿammîm kullām* 'And he said, Hear, you peoples, all of you': these words open the book of Micah (Mic 1:2) and are absent from the LXX; most commentators take them as a scribal addition identifying Mikhayehu ben Yimlah with Micah of Moresheth (Gray; Cogan). The MT is translated in full and the probable addition is noted here (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֧עַל מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד׃

i18n.en: So the king of Yisra'el and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah went up to Ramot-Gil'ad.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הִתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ וָבֹ֣א בַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לְבַ֣שׁ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּב֖וֹא בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the king of Yisra'el said to Yehoshafat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle; but you put on your robes." And the king of Yisra'el disguised himself and went into the battle.

notes.official: *hiṯḥappēś wāḇōʾ ḇammilḥāmâ* 'I will disguise myself and go into the battle' (infinitive absolutes, here with first-person sense, as in the ASV). The disguise is the king's attempt to evade the oracle.

paragraphs.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֡ם צִוָּ֣ה אֶת־שָׂרֵי֩ הָרֶ֨כֶב אֲשֶׁר־ל֜וֹ שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֚א תִּלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ אֶת־קָטֹ֖ן וְאֶת־גָּד֑וֹל כִּ֛י אִֽם־אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Now the king of Aram had commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying, "Fight neither with small nor great, but only with the king of Yisra'el."

notes.official: *śārê hārekeḇ ... šəlōšîm ûšənayim* 'the thirty-two captains of his chariots' (cf. the thirty-two kings of 20:1, 16).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וְהֵ֤מָּה אָֽמְרוּ֙ אַ֣ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיָּסֻ֥רוּ עָלָ֖יו לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם וַיִּזְעַ֖ק יְהוֹשָׁפָֽט׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Yehoshafat, that they said, "Surely it is the king of Yisra'el"; and they turned aside to fight against him; and Yehoshafat cried out.

notes.official: *wayyizʿaq yəhôšāp̄āṭ* 'and Yehoshafat cried out'; the parallel at 2 Chr 18:31 adds 'and YHWH helped him'.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּֽי־לֹא־מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ה֑וּא וַיָּשׁ֖וּבוּ מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Yisra'el, that they turned back from pursuing him.

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֙שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּכֶּה֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בֵּ֥ין הַדְּבָקִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַשִּׁרְיָ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְרַכָּב֗וֹ הֲפֹ֥ךְ יָדְךָ֛ וְהוֹצִיאֵ֥נִי מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵֽיתִי׃

i18n.en: And a certain man drew his bow at a venture and struck the king of Yisra'el between the joints of the armor; and he said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the camp, for I am badly wounded."

notes.official: *māšaḵ baqqešeṯ ləṯummô* 'drew his bow at a venture' (ASV), literally 'in his innocence', i.e. without aim. *bên haddəḇāqîm ûḇên hašširyān* 'between the joints of the armor', more exactly between the scale-plates and the breastplate. *hāḥŏlêṯî* 'I am badly wounded'. The random arrow fulfils the deliberate word of v 17.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּעֲלֶ֤ה הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הָיָ֧ה מָעֳמָ֛ד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֖ה נֹ֣כַח אֲרָ֑ם וַיָּ֣מָת בָּעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּ֥צֶק דַּֽם־הַמַּכָּ֖ה אֶל־חֵ֥יק הָרָֽכֶב׃

i18n.en: And the battle increased that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing Aram, and died at evening; and the blood of the wound ran out into the bottom of the chariot.

notes.official: *wattaʿăleh hammilḥāmâ* 'And the battle increased', literally 'went up'. *māʿŏmāḏ ... nōḵaḥ ʾărām* 'propped up ... facing Aram'. *ḥêq hārāḵeḇ* 'the bottom of the chariot', literally its 'bosom'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר הָרִנָּה֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כְּבֹ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־עִיר֖וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אַרְצֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And a cry passed throughout the camp about the going down of the sun, saying, "Every man to his city, and every man to his land."

notes.official: *hārinnâ* 'a cry', a ringing shout. *ʾîš ʾel-ʿîrô wəʾîš ʾel-ʾarṣô* 'Every man to his city, and every man to his land' (central `eretz`): the dispersal foretold in v 17.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣מָת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּב֖וֹא שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: So the king died, and was brought to Shomron; and they buried the king in Shomron.

notes.official: *wayyāmoṯ hammeleḵ wayyāḇôʾ šōmərôn* 'So the king died, and was brought to Shomron': the Hebrew verb is active, 'and he came (to Shomron)'; 'was brought' is a sense rendering, as in the ASV, for the dead king's return.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁטֹ֨ף אֶת־הָרֶ֜כֶב עַ֣ל ׀ בְּרֵכַ֣ת שֹׁמְר֗וֹן וַיָּלֹ֤קּוּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דָּמ֔וֹ וְהַזֹּנ֖וֹת רָחָ֑צוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And they washed the chariot by the pool of Shomron, and the dogs licked up his blood, and the prostitutes washed themselves, according to the word of YHWH which he spoke.

notes.official: *wayyišṭōp̄ ʾeṯ-hārekeḇ* 'And they washed the chariot' (MT singular 'he washed', impersonal). *wayyālōqqû hakkəlāḇîm ʾeṯ-dāmô* 'and the dogs licked up his blood': the fulfilment of Eliyahu's word at 21:19, though there the place is where Navot's blood was licked, and Navot's vineyard was in Yizre'el (21:1). *wəhazzōnôṯ rāḥāṣû* 'and the prostitutes washed themselves' (central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus`): Qal *rḥṣ* used intransitively, 'bathe' (Ex 2:5), as in the ASV. The LXX reads 'the pigs and the dogs licked the blood, and the prostitutes washed in the blood'; the MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י אַחְאָ֜ב וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה וּבֵ֤ית הַשֵּׁן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה וְכָל־הֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Now the rest of the acts of Ach'av, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Yisra'el?

notes.official: *ûḇêṯ haššēn* 'the ivory house', a palace with ivory inlays; carved ivories were recovered in the excavations of Samaria (Crowfoot and Crowfoot, *Early Ivories from Samaria*, 1938; cf. Amos 3:15). *sēp̄er diḇrê hayyāmîm ləmalḵê yiśrāʾēl* 'the book of the chronicles of the kings of Yisra'el', a lost source cited throughout Kings.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אַחְאָ֖ב עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So Ach'av slept with his fathers; and Achazyahu his son reigned in his place.

notes.official: 'So Ach'av slept with his fathers' (central `shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`), used here even of a king killed in battle. Achazyahu = Ahaziah. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: וִיהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ בֶּן־אָסָ֔א מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־יְהוּדָ֑ה בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֔ע לְאַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshafat the son of Asa began to reign over Yehudah in the fourth year of Ach'av king of Yisra'el.

notes.official: The regnal summary of Yehoshafat of Yehudah (vv 41-51) follows the standard Kings formula: accession synchronism, age, length of reign, mother's name, evaluation, closing notice.

paragraphs.text: יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ עֲזוּבָ֖ה בַּת־שִׁלְחִֽי׃

i18n.en: Yehoshafat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Yerushalayim. And his mother's name was Azuvah the daughter of Shilchi.

notes.official: Azuvah = Azubah; Shilchi = Shilhi.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּכָל־דֶּ֛רֶךְ אָסָ֥א אָבִ֖יו לֹא־סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of YHWH.

notes.official: Versification: MT 22:43 and 22:44 together correspond to ASV 22:43, and from here to the end the MT runs one verse ahead (MT 22:45-54 = ASV 22:44-53); MT 1 Kings ends at 22:54. The chapter keeps the MT numbering and refIds (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *lōʾ-sār mimmennû* 'he did not turn aside from it'.

paragraphs.text: אַ֥ךְ הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹֽא־סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

notes.official: *ʾaḵ habbāmôṯ lōʾ-sārû* 'Only the high places were not taken away' (13:2). MT 22:44 = ASV 22:43b (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ם יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט עִם־מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshafat made peace with the king of Yisra'el.

notes.official: MT 22:45 = ASV 22:44 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *wayyašlēm* 'made peace': the alliance of vv 2-4.

paragraphs.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט וּגְבוּרָת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחָ֑ם הֲלֹֽא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: Now the rest of the acts of Yehoshafat, and his might that he showed, and how he warred, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Yehudah?

notes.official: MT 22:46 = ASV 22:45 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְיֶ֙תֶר֙ הַקָּדֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאַ֔ר בִּימֵ֖י אָסָ֣א אָבִ֑יו בִּעֵ֖ר מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And the remnant of the qadesh, who remained in the days of his father Asa, he put away out of the land.

notes.official: *wəyeṯer haqqāḏēš* 'And the remnant of the qadesh' (ASV 'the sodomites'). *qāḏēš*, here a collective singular, is a male cultic functionary attached to a sanctuary ('consecrated one', from *qdš*); whether the role was sexual is disputed (Bird, *Missing Persons and Mistaken Identities*, 1997; Budin, *The Myth of Sacred Prostitution in Antiquity*, 2008). The ASV 'sodomites' imports a link with Sodom and modern senses that the Hebrew does not carry. The translation transliterates, following the central `qedeshah-consecrated-woman-sacred-prostitution-crux`, which names this verse among the sites it governs and renders the feminine 'qedeshah' at Gen 38:21-22. The same reform is reported of Asa at 15:12. *biʿēr min-hāʾāreṣ* 'he put away out of the land' (central `eretz`). MT 22:47 = ASV 22:46 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֵ֛ין בֶּאֱד֖וֹם נִצָּ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And there was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.

notes.official: *ûmeleḵ ʾên beʾĕḏôm niṣṣāḇ meleḵ* 'And there was no king in Edom; a deputy was king' (ASV). *niṣṣāḇ* is a 'prefect, deputy' (cf. 4:5, 7). The clause explains how Yehoshafat could build ships at Etzyon-Gever on Edomite territory (v 49): Edom was governed by an appointee of Yehudah until its revolt (2 Kgs 8:20). Some read 'a deputy of the king'. ASV kept. MT 22:48 = ASV 22:47 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט עשר [עָשָׂה֩] אֳנִיּ֨וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֜ישׁ לָלֶ֧כֶת אוֹפִ֛ירָה לַזָּהָ֖ב וְלֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־נשברה [נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ] אֳנִיּ֖וֹת בְּעֶצְי֥וֹן גָּֽבֶר׃

i18n.en: Yehoshafat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold; but they did not go, for the ships were broken at Etzyon-Gever.

notes.official: Two Ketiv/Qere pairs: Ketiv *ʿśr* (readable as *ʿeśer* 'ten' [ships]), Qere *ʿāśâ* 'made'; Ketiv *nšbrh* (feminine singular 'was broken'), Qere *nišbərû* (plural 'were broken'). Both Qere readings are translated, as in the ASV (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *ʾŏniyyôṯ taršîš* 'ships of Tarshish', large seagoing ships named after the distant port. Ophir = the gold-land of 9:28; Etzyon-Gever = Ezion-geber, on the Gulf of Aqaba. *wəlōʾ hālāḵ* 'but they did not go' (MT singular, collective). MT 22:49 = ASV 22:48 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: אָ֠ז אָמַ֞ר אֲחַזְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־אַחְאָב֙ אֶל־יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט יֵלְכ֧וּ עֲבָדַ֛י עִם־עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בָּאֳנִיּ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה יְהוֹשָׁפָֽט׃

i18n.en: Then Achazyahu the son of Ach'av said to Yehoshafat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Yehoshafat would not.

notes.official: MT 22:50 = ASV 22:49 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). 2 Chr 20:35-37 tells the episode differently: Yehoshafat joins Achazyahu and is rebuked for it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵר֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Yehoshafat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Yehoram his son reigned in his place.

notes.official: Yehoram = Jehoram. 'slept with his fathers' (central `shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`). MT 22:51 = ASV 22:50 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). The Masoretic section mark (ס) follows.

paragraphs.text: אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַ֣ע עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Achazyahu the son of Ach'av began to reign over Yisra'el in Shomron in the seventeenth year of Yehoshafat king of Yehudah, and he reigned two years over Yisra'el.

notes.official: MT 22:52 = ASV 22:51 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). Achazyahu's two-year reign continues into 2 Kgs 1.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אָבִיו֙ וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ אִמּ֔וֹ וּבְדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And he did what was evil in the eyes of YHWH, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Yarov'am the son of Nevat, who made Yisra'el to sin.

notes.official: MT 22:53 = ASV 22:52 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *ûḇəḏereḵ ʾimmô* 'and in the way of his mother', Izevel. Nevat = Nebat; *ʾăšer heḥĕṭîʾ ʾeṯ-yiśrāʾēl* 'who made Yisra'el to sin', the refrain that begins at 13:34.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֔עַל וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה ל֑וֹ וַיַּכְעֵ֗ס אֶת־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he served Ba'al and bowed down to him, and provoked YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, to anger, according to all that his father had done.

notes.official: *wayyaʿăḇōḏ ʾeṯ-habbaʿal* 'And he served Ba'al': the Hebrew writes the name with the article (*habbaʿal*), which English, like the ASV, omits (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-kings`; as at 18:19-40). 'YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (central `elohei-yisrael`). MT 22:54 = ASV 22:53, the last verse of 1 Kings (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`); the Achazyahu narrative continues in 2 Kgs 1.
